sec: Excretion, stone thresholds, milk-alkali syndrome and renal handling · p875

items.q: Daily urinary calcium loss is approximately:
items.exp: ~200 mg lost in urine; 4 mg/kg/24 hours; >4 mg/kg/day = hypercalciuria. (Book p875)

items.q: Match the ‘4/7/11’ stone thresholds — 1) >4 mg/kg/24 hr  2) >7 mg/24 hr  3) <11 mg/kg/24 hr … A) Hyperuricosuria (2nd m/c)  B) Hypocitraturia  C) Hypercalciuria (m/c)
items.exp: m/c causes of stones: hypercalciuria >4 mg/kg/24 hr (m/c), hyperuricosuria >7 mg/24 hr (2nd m/c), hypocitraturia <11 mg/kg/24 hr. (Book p875)

items.q: Milk-alkali syndrome begins with excess calcium consumption above:
items.exp: Excess Ca2+ consumption >4 g/day → ↑ paracellular Ca2+ entry. (Book p875)

items.q: In milk-alkali syndrome, hypercalcaemia activates CaSR which then:
opts: Reduces Ca2+ absorption and ADH → volume depletion → RAAS → metabolic alkalosis
items.exp: Hypercalcaemia (+) CaSR (−) → ↓ Ca2+ absorption and ↓ ADH → volume depletion → RAAS → metabolic alkalosis; also hypercalciuria → stones. (Book p875)

items.q: Match renal calcium handling — 1) PCT  2) TAL  3) DCT … A) 25%, paracellular, PTH-dependent  B) 10%, active transport, most dependent  C) 65%, paracellular, PTH-independent
items.exp: PCT 65% paracellular independent; TAL 25% paracellular dependent; DCT 10% active transport most dependent. (Book p875)

items.q: A rise in ionized calcium triggers, within SECONDS, the:
opts: Parathyroid CaSR inhibiting PTH release → hypocalcaemia (immediate response)
items.exp: Within seconds: parathyroid CaSR (−) PTH release → hypocalcaemia (immediate). (Book p875)

items.q: Within a FEW DAYS, raised ionized calcium acts on the kidney (TAL) CaSR to cause:
items.exp: Delayed response: kidney (TAL) CaSR (−) Ca2+ reabsorption → hypercalciuria; vice-versa when ionized calcium falls. (Book p875)

items.q: In the TAL diagram, the claudins shown regulating paracellular calcium are:
items.exp: TAL regulation involves CLDN 16/19 and claudin-14, with PTH raising absorption and CaSR raising excretion. (Book p875)
